paper.title_en: Connecting the little dots in polarized light
paper.abstract_en: Recent observations of the local Little Red Dot (LRD) analog SDSS~J1025+1402 have revealed that the optical continuum is polarized at the ~1.5% level, while broad Halpha has lower polarization (~0.7%) and a different polarization angle. We investigate whether these properties can be reproduced in a scenario in which LRDs are dust-obscured Little Blue Dots (LBDs) viewed at high inclination and powered by super-Eddington accretion. In this framework, electron scattering in the geometrically thick inner accretion flow produces intrinsic continuum polarization, while unpolarized emission from the outer thin disk dilutes the signal, particularly at optical wavelengths. Broad Halpha, which is emitted outside the compact disk atmosphere, lacks this intrinsic disk-atmosphere polarization. A circumnuclear dust screen then contributes dichroic polarization to both the continuum and broad-line emission, producing the lower line polarization and its different position angle. We show that this model reproduces the main observed polarization properties, although degeneracies between accretion rate and inclination remain. Standard equatorial- and polar-scattering AGN polarization models fail to reproduce the observed continuum and broad-line polarization simultaneously. These results illustrate the potential of spectropolarimetry as a probe of accretion-flow geometry and orientation in the little-dot population, complementary to spectral-energy-distribution fitting and line diagnostics.
